subject: Post-call: Hosting route decision & BAA evidence gap list
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Aaron Patel <aaron@mediva.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 17:15:00 -0400
Subject: Post-call: Hosting route decision & BAA evidence gap list

Hi Aaron / Mediva security team —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the hosting route and the compliance evidence you asked for.

Call summary (high level)
- Primary constraint: PHI processing for appointment reminders and clinical summaries -> BAA required.
- Preference stated: Private VPC if we can meet your audit windows; fallback to Dedicated (reserved) if timeline/cost forces it. Hosted API accepted only for non-PHI lanes.
- SOC 2: You asked for the usual artifact set (attestation, user access controls, network diagrams, change-control evidence) plus runtime logs for a 30-day window.

Immediate asks / action items
1) Mediva: confirm whether 1) you require customer-managed keys (BYOK) for keys in the BAA scope, and 2) whether 3rd-party auditors must be granted direct access for on-site checks or if remote evidence is acceptable. Reply requested by EOD Mon 4/26.
2) Redwood (Karthik): provide high-level runbook and timeline for Private VPC provisioning (network peering, VPN setup, expected lead time), and list any audit blockers. Target: 4/23 EOD.
3) Redwood (Marissa): share the SOC 2 artifact checklist and a redlined BAA template. Target: 4/23 noon.

Attachments I uploaded to the shared drive: SOC2-questionnaire.xlsx (master checklist), Redwood_BAA_template_v2.docx (redlineable). Link below.

If Mediva is leaning Private VPC, the biggest open items for us to plan resourcing are: KMS/BYOK decision, audit access model, and expected go-live (are we aiming for pilot with non-production PHI in June?).

Next meeting suggestion: 30-min sync week of 4/26 to lock the route and kickoff the provisioning sprint. I’ll send a calendar invite once Aaron confirms preferred times.

Thanks —
Priya Natarajan

Priya —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from our side:
1) BYOK: Preferred, yes. We need separation of keys for PHI workloads. If Redwood cannot support customer-managed keys in Private VPC by pilot, we can accept Redwood-managed keys but will require an SLA and key rotation proof.
2) Auditor access: Remote evidence is acceptable for initial assessments; we reserve the right for on-site reviews annually.
3) Timeline: target pilot start is June 7 (non-production PHI), production targeted for late Q3.

We’ve attached the Mediva SOC intake (short form) and our legal note about audit windows. Also flagging that our procurement lead may request sample data retention settings — we retain certain logs for 7 years, but we can discuss scoping.

Next steps from our side: I’ll confirm BYOK decision authority by Monday and loop procurement if we need a longer retention conversation.

—Aaron

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Hosting route decision & BAA evidence gap list

Aaron / Priya —

Thanks — quick technical readout on Private VPC feasibility and items that will affect timeline/cost:

Feasibility and lead times
- Private VPC (preferred): supported. Typical provisioning for a new VPC + peering + VPN and network hardening: 3–4 business days for initial sandbox environment, 2–3 weeks for hardened production (we do an infra change window and security validation).
- Dedicated (reserved gpu pool): ~5 business days to reserve nodes, faster but does not provide tenant VPC isolation (we isolate at the network layer).
- Hosted API w/ BAA scoping: possible only for non-PHI or heavily redacted PHI flows; not ideal for full PHI workloads given audit requirements.

Open technical questions that change delivery
- BYOK model: we support both Redwood-managed and customer-managed keys in our Private offering; if Mediva wants HSM-backed BYOK with customer HSM hosting (on-prem KMS), that adds ~2 weeks for integration and a short security review. Please confirm whether the BYOK must be HSM-backed.
- Audit evidence: We can provide network diagrams, SCPs, runbooks, config snapshots, and tokenized runtime logs for 30 days. If Mediva requires raw runtime logs beyond 90 days or 7-year retention on audit logs, that will require a retention addon (cost add).

Proposed interim plan
1) Redwood to provision a sandbox Private VPC environment week of 4/26 (sandbox = no PHI) so security can validate network controls.
2) If sandbox passes, schedule production provisioning sprint (2–3 week lead time) with an audit window on our side.
3) Marissa to share SOC2 artifacts and redlined BAA by EOD 4/23.

I attached a short checklist of technical artifacts we’ll produce for your auditor (SOC2 attestation, network diagram, access matrix, runbook). I’ll also prepare a short KMS/BYOK notes doc if you want more detail.

-Karthik
